subject.title: Subagent-completion wake on the internal channel bypasses the silent-reply allowance, and the empty-response re-nudge can leak injected instructions to the user channel

question: Should this prompt-directive disclosure remain a public bug fix, or be routed through the private security-advisory process while the affected content and release range are assessed?
rationale: The implementation direction is narrow, but the report alleges real user-channel disclosure of injected directives, so maintainers should determine the appropriate disclosure and release-handling boundary.

options.title: Security-route and patch
options.body: Privately assess the disclosure scope, then land the narrow policy-aware fix and regression coverage with an appropriate coordinated release.

options.title: Treat as public reliability bug
options.body: Keep the issue public and land the same narrow fix after confirming that exposed directives cannot include secrets or privileged data.

recommendation.title: Security-route and patch
recommendation.body: Privately assess the disclosure scope, then land the narrow policy-aware fix and regression coverage with an appropriate coordinated release.
